summary: Lindsay G. McCune works in the fields of Tibetology and religious studies. McCune studied under MA supervisor Bryan J. Cuevas, as attested in 2007, as well as under teachers Kathleen M. Erndl and John Corrigan.
Lindy Li Mark works in Sinology and other fields. Mark held positions as professor of anthropology at California State University, East Bay, and at The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
Ling Ji is a scholar in Sinology who completed a PhD at the National University of Singapore, attested in 2014, under the supervision of Chi Xiao and Yuet Keung Lo.

Linnart Mäll (1938–2010) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Tartu (~1957–1964) and under traditional teacher Bidia Dandaron (~1968–1972), later holding a post at the University of Tartu (~1969–2010).

Lionel David Barnett (1871–1960) was an Indologist who studied at the University of Liverpool (~1888–1892) and Trinity College, Cambridge (~1892–1896). He served at the British Museum (1899–1948), University College London (1906–1917), and SOAS (1917–1948).

Lionel Obadia (born 1969) is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies. After earning a PhD from Lille University of Science and Technology in 1997, he held posts at INALCO, KU Leuven, EPHE, Lille 3 University, and Lyon 2.

Liqian Liu (1910–2008) worked in Tibetology. He held posts at West China Union University (~1944–1949), the State Council of the People's Republic of China translation administration department (~1952–1959), and the Ethnic Publishing House (~1959–1978).

Lisa Grumbach works in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. She held a post at Stanford University, attested in 1996, and served as an assistant professor at the Institute of Buddhist Studies.

Lisa N. Owen specializes in Indology, history and archaeology, and religious studies. She studied under Walter M. Spink in 1995 and completed her Ph.D. at the University of Texas at Austin under the supervision of Janice Leoshko.
Lita Peipina is a scholar of Buddhist studies. She studied under Jens-Uwe Hartmann and Jens Braarvig, completing an MA at the University of Oslo, attested in 2008.

Liu Zaifu (1941–2026) was a scholar in Sinology and philosophy. After studying at Xiamen University (~1959–1963), he worked at CASS (1963, 1985–1989), and held posts at Chicago, Colorado, Stockholm, City University of Hong Kong, and HKUST.

Lloyd W. Pflueger is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He earned a doctorate at the University of California, Santa Barbara, and served as Professor of Philosophy and Religion at Truman State University, attested in 2015.

Lobsang Dargyay (1935–1994) was a scholar in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Rahor Monastery, Drepung Monastery (~1952–1959), and the University of Munich (~1969–1974), where he earned his Dr.phil.

Lobsang Gyatso (1928–1997) studied at Drepung Monastery (~1940–1959) and under Tendzin Chökyi Gyatso in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He founded the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics (1973), heading it from ~1973 to 1997, and founded the College for Higher Tibetan Studies (1991).

Lobsang Phuntshok Lhalungpa (1926–2008) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under numerous teachers, including Dudjom Rinpoche, Trijang Rinpoche, Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, and Drubwang Shakya Shri, and later taught John W. Pettit.

Lobsang Shastri is a scholar in Tibetology. Shastri served as Head Librarian of the Tibetan Section at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives, attested 2003–2006, and as Senior Librarian at the Buddhist Digital Resource Center, attested in 2018.
Lobsang Tenpa is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Tenpa earned a Master of Philosophy degree at Jawaharlal Nehru University under the supervision of Sharad K. Soni.

Lobsang Tenzin (born 1937) is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar educated at Drepung Monastery. He served as abbot of Gyume Tantric Monastery, Principal and Director of CIHTS, President of the Association of Indian Universities, and Chancellor of Sanchi University.

Lobsang Yongdan works in Tibetology and history and archaeology. He studied at Kumbum Monastery and completed a PhD at the University of Cambridge by 2014 under Hildegard Diemberger, later holding postdoctoral posts at MPIWG and the University of Bonn.

Loden Sherab Dagyab (born 1940) is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Drepung Monastery and under Tenzin Gyatso, Trijang Rinpoche, and Ling Rinpoche. He directed Tibet House, New Delhi (1964–1966) and served at the University of Bonn.
